D65·b154 — 2026-10-19
chose: 8.3: only HEAVY gates take the machine-wide verify slot: the full --verify, a task's own plan verify, and decision checks. A tiered run's quick-tier check (vitest related on a task's files) takes no slot. A waiter no longer barges after one command timeout. It waits while the holder is inside its own declared bound, read from an advisory sidecar <state base>/verify.lock.json ({started_at, bound_ms, command, initiative}) that the holder writes on claim and removes on release. It barges with a warning only when that holder overruns its bound by SLOT_GRACE_MS, or when the whole wait passes SLOT_QUEUE_FACTOR (6) × its timeout. The flock alone still decides liveness.
over: keeping the barge after timeoutMs, which let 9 queued full suites run at once and time each other out; an unbounded wait (session-driver D10: no state an unattended run can sit in forever); holder metadata inside the lock file (drive-visibility D2 keeps it empty and pid-free); a FIFO queue directory (needs cleanup of dead entries, which only the lock can answer)
because: A gate's timeout clock starts only after it claims the slot, so a queued waiter loses nothing by waiting, while a barge both overloads the machine and burns the holder's timeout. A holder's command is bounded by its own timeout, so waiting on a live in-bound holder is bounded per holder. The queue cap bounds starvation, since flock is not fair. Quick checks are cheap by design (8.2), and queueing them behind full suites would cost what tiering saved.
